MCQs.question: Which body system is made of bones, joints and cartilage?
Which blood vessels take blood out of the heart to the rest of the body?
Which of these gives out its own light?
Which disease is caused by a fungus?

In the chain grass, rabbit, fox, what will most likely happen to the fox if all the rabbits disappear?
options: a) It will start eating grass
c) It will struggle to find enough to eat
d) It will become a producer
MCQs.answer: c) It will struggle to find enough to eat

MCQs.question: Which of these is a producer?
Which of these will stay in a garden for years without breaking down?

Label the Diagram.question: The Human Respiratory System
Label the Diagram.answer: 1. Nasal cavity, 2. Larynx, 3. Trachea, 4. Lung, 5. Diaphragm

points.text: Nasal cavity labelled correctly
Larynx labelled correctly
Trachea labelled correctly
Lung labelled correctly
Diaphragm labelled correctly

accept: Windpipe for trachea
Voice box for larynx
Right lung or left lung for lung
scheme.common_error: Writing pharynx or bronchus for the larynx or trachea, or mixing up the lung and the diaphragm.

Draw and Label.main_question: Draw the diagram named below in the space given and label its parts. Answer any ONE.
Draw and Label.question: Draw and label the Respiratory System. Label at least 7 parts.
Draw and Label.answer: A neat drawing of the respiratory system with 7 labels from: nose (nasal cavity), mouth, throat, voice box, windpipe, right lung, left lung, diaphragm.

points.text: Drawing shows a recognisable respiratory system with the lungs and windpipe in the correct places
Seven parts labelled correctly, 5 marks for the 7 labels (a mark for each correct label, up to 5)

accept: Nose, mouth, throat, voice box, windpipe, right lung, left lung
Nasal cavity, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchus, lungs, diaphragm
scheme.common_error: Placing the lungs outside the chest, or mixing up the windpipe with the food pipe.

Draw and Label.main_question: Draw the diagram named below in the space given and label its parts. Answer any ONE.
Draw and Label.question: Draw and label a Food Chain of four living things, starting with a plant. Label 4 parts.
Draw and Label.answer: A food chain of four living things such as grass, grasshopper, mouse, snake, with the producer first and the labels: producer, primary consumer, secondary consumer, and the last consumer.

points.text: Four living things drawn or named in a correct feeding order, starting with a plant
Four labels given correctly (a mark for each correct label)

accept: Grass, grasshopper, mouse, snake with producer, primary consumer, secondary consumer, consumer labels
Grass, rabbit, fox, hawk with producer and consumer labels
scheme.common_error: Starting the chain with an animal or placing the living things in the wrong feeding order.

Logical Reasoning.main_question: Give answers with logical reasons. Answer any TWO of the three questions.
Logical Reasoning.question: Rani added a spoonful of sugar to a glass of water and stirred. The sugar seemed to vanish and the water tasted sweet. Then Rani left the water in a warm sunny place for several days until all the water was gone.

questions.question: Why did the sugar seem to vanish in the water?
questions.answer: The sugar broke into tiny particles that mixed with the water, so we cannot see them, but it is still sugar.

points.text: States the sugar dissolves or breaks into tiny particles and spreads in the water
States it is still there / no new substance forms

accept: It dissolved and is still sugar, just too small to see
scheme.common_error: Saying the sugar was destroyed or turned into a new substance.

questions.question: What do you think Rani will find in the glass after the water is gone? Why?
questions.answer: Sugar will be left, because only the water dried up and the sugar stayed.

points.text: Says the sugar is left behind
Gives the reason that only the water went away

accept: Sugar crystals, because the water dried but the sugar stays
scheme.common_error: Saying nothing will be left because the sugar vanished.

questions.question: Is dissolving sugar in water a change that can be reversed? Explain.
questions.answer: Yes, because the sugar can be got back by drying up the water, since no new substance was made.

points.text: Says yes, it can be reversed
Reason: the water can be dried up to get the sugar back / no new substance formed

accept: Yes, it is a physical change and drying the water brings back the sugar
scheme.common_error: Saying it cannot be reversed because the sugar disappeared.

accept: Any two of the three sub-questions answered correctly
scheme.common_error: Thinking dissolved sugar is gone for good.

Logical Reasoning.main_question: Give answers with logical reasons. Answer any TWO of the three questions.
Logical Reasoning.question: Jojo left an iron nail in a jar of plain water and another iron nail in a jar of salty water. After a few days both nails had turned orange, but the nail in salty water was much more orange. Jojo also burned a small piece of paper and saw it turn into black ash.

questions.question: Why did the nails change colour?
questions.answer: The iron reacted with water and air (oxygen) and formed rust, which is a new substance.

points.text: States that iron meets water and oxygen (air)
States that rust, a new substance, formed

accept: Rusting because of water and air
scheme.common_error: Saying the water only coloured the nail orange.

questions.question: What does the nail in salty water tell Jojo about how salt affects the change?
questions.answer: Salt makes the rusting happen faster.

points.text: States that salt speeds up rusting
Compares with the plain water nail

accept: Rust forms quicker in salty water than in plain water
scheme.common_error: Saying salt stops rusting.

questions.question: Jojo says burning paper and rusting are the same kind of change. Do you agree? Give a reason.
questions.answer: Yes, both are chemical changes because a new substance forms (ash or rust) that cannot easily be changed back.

points.text: Agrees that both are chemical changes
Reason: a new substance forms in each / cannot be reversed

accept: Yes, new substances (ash and rust) are made
scheme.common_error: Calling burning a physical change because the paper changes shape.

accept: Any two of the three sub-questions answered correctly
scheme.common_error: Treating colour change as always a physical change.

Logical Reasoning.main_question: Give answers with logical reasons. Answer any TWO of the three questions.
Logical Reasoning.question: Gul Rukh pointed a torch at a wall and placed three things in front of it one by one: a clear drinking glass, a frosted plastic cup and a ceramic mug. She saw a faint shadow with the glass, a darker shadow with the cup and a solid black shadow with the mug.

questions.question: Why did the mug make a solid black shadow?
questions.answer: The mug is opaque, so it blocks all the light.

points.text: Says the mug is opaque
Says it blocks all the light

accept: It does not let any light pass through
scheme.common_error: Saying the mug makes its own light.

questions.question: Why was the shadow of the frosted cup darker than the shadow of the glass?
questions.answer: The frosted cup is translucent and lets only some light through, while the clear glass lets most light pass.

points.text: Says the cup lets only some light pass and scatters it
Says the glass lets more light pass

accept: Translucent materials block more light than transparent ones
scheme.common_error: Saying the cup blocks all light.

questions.question: Gul Rukh wants to look at a friend through a thin sheet but wants the friend to look blurry. Which kind of material should she choose? Why?
questions.answer: A translucent material, such as tissue paper, because it lets light through but scatters it so things look blurry.

points.text: Chooses a translucent material
Reason: light passes but is scattered, so the view is blurry

accept: Tissue paper or frosted plastic, because it scatters light
scheme.common_error: Choosing an opaque material, through which nothing can be seen.

accept: Any two of the three sub-questions answered correctly
scheme.common_error: Mixing up translucent and transparent.

Brief Answers.question: Name the three main parts of the circulatory system and state what the heart does.
Brief Answers.answer: The heart, the blood vessels and the blood. The heart is a pump that pushes blood around the body.

points.text: Names the three parts: heart, blood vessels, blood (1 mark each)
States that the heart is a pump that pushes blood around the body

accept: Arteries and veins given for blood vessels
The heart pumps blood to all parts of the body
scheme.common_error: Naming the lungs or the stomach as a part of the circulatory system.

Brief Answers.question: Explain how the skeletal system helps our body.
Brief Answers.answer: Bones support the body and help us stand straight. Bones and joints help us move, walk and play. The skeleton also protects inner parts such as the heart and lungs.

points.text: Supports the body and helps us stand straight
Bones and joints help us move
Protects inner organs such as the heart and lungs

accept: Gives the body its shape and framework
scheme.common_error: Saying the skeleton pumps blood or digests meals.

Brief Answers.question: Define the word vaccine.
Brief Answers.answer: A vaccine is an injection, liquid, pill or nasal spray that teaches the immune system to recognise and defend against disease-causing germs.

points.text: It is given as an injection, liquid, pill or nasal spray
It teaches the immune system to recognise and defend against disease-causing germs

accept: Giving a vaccine makes a person immune to a disease
scheme.common_error: Saying a vaccine is a medicine that cures a disease immediately.

Brief Answers.question: Explain how yeast helps dough become fluffy bread.
Brief Answers.answer: Yeast is a fungus. When it is mixed in dough it ferments the sugar and gives off carbon dioxide gas. The gas makes the dough rise and become fluffy.

points.text: Yeast is a fungus
Yeast ferments or changes the sugar in the dough
It gives off carbon dioxide gas
The gas makes the bread rise and become fluffy

accept: Gas bubbles get trapped in the dough
scheme.common_error: Saying yeast is a bacterium or that heat alone makes the bread rise.

Brief Answers.question: A factory pours waste into a river. A cow drinks water from the river. Explain how the waste can end up affecting a family who eat the cow's meat.
Brief Answers.answer: The waste pollutes the river water and makes plants and fish ill. The cow drinks the polluted water, so the pollutants enter its body. When the family eats the meat, the pollutants pass to them and can cause diseases.

points.text: The waste pollutes the river water and affects plants and fish
The cow drinks the water and the pollutants pass into its body
The family eats the meat and the pollutants pass to them
This can make them ill or cause diseases

accept: Pollutants move along the feeding links from the water to the cow to humans
scheme.common_error: Saying the waste stays in the river and cannot reach the family.

Brief Answers.question: Name three fossil fuels and one greenhouse gas that is released when they burn. What do greenhouse gases do to the Sun's heat?
Brief Answers.answer: Coal, oil and natural gas. Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas. Greenhouse gases trap the Sun's heat in the lower atmosphere.

points.text: Names three fossil fuels (1 mark each)
Names a greenhouse gas such as carbon dioxide
Greenhouse gases trap the Sun's heat

accept: Kerosene or propane as a fossil fuel
scheme.common_error: Naming wood or paper as fossil fuels.

Brief Answers.question: Explain the difference between a conductor and an insulator. Give one example of each.
Brief Answers.answer: A conductor lets electric current flow easily, for example copper wire, so a bulb in the circuit lights up. An insulator does not let current flow, for example wood or plastic, so it breaks the circuit.

points.text: A conductor allows electric current to flow easily
A correct example of a conductor, such as a metal wire or coin
An insulator does not allow current to flow
A correct example of an insulator, such as wood or plastic
A conductor completes a circuit so the bulb lights, while an insulator does not

accept: Aluminium foil or a paper clip as a conductor
Rubber as an insulator
scheme.common_error: Saying an insulator is a metal.

Brief Answers.question: Explain why rusting of an iron nail is a chemical change.
Brief Answers.answer: An iron nail left in air and water slowly turns into a flaky orange-red coating called rust. Rust is a new material with different properties from iron. It cannot easily be turned back, so it is a chemical change.

points.text: Iron reacts with air and water
An orange-red flaky coating forms
A new material with different properties is formed
The change cannot be easily reversed

accept: The nail changes colour and weakens and a new product is made
scheme.common_error: Saying the nail only changes shape or appearance, so it is a physical change.

Brief Answers.question: A child looks at a torch light behind a frosted plastic cup and sees only a blurry glow. Is the cup transparent, translucent or opaque? Give a reason.
Brief Answers.answer: The cup is translucent. It lets some light pass but scatters it, so the torch looks blurry and not clear.

points.text: Translucent
It lets some light pass
It scatters the light, so things behind look blurry or unclear

accept: Not transparent because the torch is not seen clearly, and not opaque because some light gets by
scheme.common_error: Calling the cup transparent because some light passes.

Brief Answers.question: Jojo joins a battery, a bulb and wires, but leaves a gap between two nails in the circuit. A wooden stick lies across the gap and the bulb stays off. Explain why the bulb is off and how Jojo can make it light.
Brief Answers.answer: Wood is an insulator, so current cannot flow across the gap. The circuit has a break, so it is open. Jojo can place a steel paper clip across both nails to close the circuit and the bulb will light.

points.text: Wood is an insulator and does not let current flow
The circuit has a break, so it is an open circuit
Joining the nails with a conductor such as a paper clip closes the circuit so the bulb lights

accept: Any metal object that touches both nails
scheme.common_error: Saying the bulb is off because the battery is the wrong way round.

Long Question.main_question: Answer the following questions in detail.
Long Question.question: Explain how contagious diseases such as COVID-19 and polio spread from one person to another, and describe the ways we can stop them from spreading.
Long Question.answer: COVID-19 spreads mainly by droplets in the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes. Polio can spread by contaminated water. Diseases also spread by touch, handshakes, hugs and shared surfaces. We can wear masks, wash hands with soap and water, keep our distance, use sanitisers and avoid body contact.

points.text: COVID-19 spreads by airborne droplets from coughs and sneezes
Polio can spread by contaminated water
Germs also spread by touch, handshakes, hugs or shared surfaces
Wearing masks
Washing hands thoroughly with soap and water
Keeping distance from sick persons
Using sanitisers and avoiding body contact

accept: Drinking only clean water as a way to stop polio spreading
Staying at home when ill
scheme.common_error: Saying COVID-19 spreads only by contaminated water.

Long Question.main_question: Answer the following questions in detail.
Long Question.question: Explain how burning fossil fuels in cars and factories leads to global warming.
Long Question.answer: Cars, factories and power plants burn fossil fuels. Burning releases greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide into the air. These gases trap the Sun's heat in the lower atmosphere, which is called the greenhouse effect. The extra trapped heat warms the Earth, causing global warming and climate change. This changes weather patterns and affects ecosystems everywhere.

points.text: Fossil fuels are burned in cars, factories and power plants
Burning releases greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide
The gases trap the Sun's heat in the lower atmosphere
This is called the greenhouse effect
It causes global warming and climate change
Weather patterns and ecosystems are affected

accept: The Earth's temperature rises because heat cannot escape
scheme.common_error: Saying greenhouse gases make the Sun hotter.

Long Question.main_question: Answer the following questions in detail.
Long Question.question: Explain how noise pollution affects humans and animals and what we can do to reduce it.
Long Question.answer: Noise pollution is loud, unwanted noise. It can cause sleep problems, headaches, high blood pressure and problems with memory and attention, and it can damage hearing. Animals can hear even louder noises than humans, so they are affected too. We can keep the volume low, avoid blowing horns, use silencers, wear earmuffs or earplugs in noisy places and switch off appliances we do not use.

points.text: Causes sleep problems
Causes headaches
Causes high blood pressure
Causes problems with memory and attention
Can damage hearing, including that of animals
Keep the volume of television or music low
Avoid blowing vehicle horns and use silencers
Wear earmuffs or earplugs in noisy areas
Switch off electronic appliances not in use

accept: Speak in a normal voice in crowded rooms
Ask for rules to control noise
scheme.common_error: Saying only humans are affected by noise.

Long Question.main_question: Answer the following questions in detail.
Long Question.question: Rani strokes a sewing needle about forty times with one end of a magnet in the same direction. She fixes it on a cork and floats it in a bowl of water. Explain why the needle becomes a magnet and why it slowly turns to point north.
Long Question.answer: Iron has tiny magnets inside pointing in random directions. Stroking with a magnet in one direction lines them up, so the needle becomes a temporary magnet. On the floating cork it turns freely. The Earth acts like a giant magnet, so the needle's north end is pulled to the magnetic north. After a while the tiny magnets get jumbled and the needle stops being a magnet.

points.text: Stroking in one direction many times with the same end of the magnet
The tiny magnets inside the needle line up in the same direction
The needle becomes a temporary magnet
The cork lets the needle turn freely on water
The Earth acts like a giant magnet with its own magnetic force
The needle's north end points to the Earth's magnetic north
The magnetism fades after a while

accept: The needle behaves like the needle in a real compass
scheme.common_error: Saying the needle points north because the water pushes it.

Long Question.main_question: Answer the following questions in detail.
Long Question.question: The rubbish dump near Taleemabad is growing quickly. Explain how sorting waste, recycling and choosing biodegradable items could slow its growth.
Long Question.answer: Biodegradable waste such as fruit peels and paper breaks down naturally and goes back to the soil. Non-biodegradable waste such as plastic and metal stays for years, so the dump grows. If we sort waste, the biodegradable part can be made into compost and the rest can be recycled. Recycling reuses materials, so less waste reaches the dump, and recycling paper also saves trees. Using substitutes for plastic items and reusing things reduces waste, which keeps the land cleaner and protects wildlife.

points.text: Biodegradable waste such as peels and paper breaks down naturally
Non-biodegradable waste such as plastic and metal stays for many years
Recycling reuses materials so less waste goes to the dump
Sorting separates waste so it can be composted or recycled
Using substitutes for plastic items or reusing things reduces waste
Less land pollution and less damage to wildlife

accept: Making compost from vegetable scraps
scheme.common_error: Saying that burying plastic makes it break down quickly.

grain.kind: one concept per item across chapters 1–6: body systems, diseases, food chains, pollution, physical and chemical change, light, sound, magnets, circuits

Detailed respiratory (alveoli) or circulatory (chambers, valves) knowledge is not required. An item never states a marking point of a Section C answer. No MCQ tests a concept that a Section B or Section C question of this paper asks, and no stem or option states a fact that a later question asks the child to explain. Each concept (physical or chemical change, vaccines, light and materials) is asked at most twice in the whole paper, never by two items of one section; a stem never states another item's answer.
